Further tightening of credit standards for loans to firms and consumer credit, owing to higher risks
Decline in loan demand across all segments, driven mainly by higher interest rates
Gradual but sustained increase in demand for loans to finance AI infrastructure
According to the October 2026 bank lending survey (BLS), euro area banks reported a further net tightening of credit standards – banks’ internal guidelines or loan approval criteria – for loans or credit lines to enterprises in the third quarter of 2026 (net percentage of 9% of banks; Chart 1). Banks reported unchanged credit standards for loans to households for house purchase (net percentage of 0%) and a further net tightening for consumer credit and other lending to households (net percentage of 14%).
For firms, the net tightening surpassed the expectations reported by banks in the previous survey round (5%). Heightened risk perceptions and banks’ reduced risk tolerance remained the main drivers of tighter credit standards, with some banks reporting increasing pressure as a result of geopolitical uncertainty and energy developments. In a dedicated question on the importance of new lending to finance firms’ adoption or development of artificial intelligence (AI), banks indicated that they are still adapting their lending practices to the growing use of these technologies. Most reported that they had not yet introduced specific quantitative criteria for assessing AI-related lending within their credit standards. A small number noted that AI adoption and its associated risks increasingly feature in qualitative borrower assessments, with IT firms subject to the closest scrutiny. Banks reported broadly unchanged credit standards for housing loans and a further net tightening of credit standards for consumer credit. For housing loans, banks had expected a slight net tightening. Meanwhile, the tightening of credit standards for consumer credit exceeded banks’ expectations, owing mainly to lower risk tolerance and heightened risk perceptions. For the fourth quarter of 2026, banks expect credit standards to tighten further for firms and tighten significantly for both housing loans and consumer credit.
Banks’ overall terms and conditions – the actual terms and conditions agreed in loan contracts – tightened for all loan segments, driven mainly by higher interest rates.
Banks reported a net increase in the share of rejected loan applications for all borrower groups. The net increase in the share was higher for consumer credit than for loans to firms and housing loans.
In the third quarter of 2026, euro area banks reported a net decrease in demand for loans or credit lines to firms (net percentage of -6%; Chart 2). This net decline stood in contrast to banks’ expectations of an increase in the previous survey round (4%) and followed a small net increase in the second quarter (3%). Loan demand was primarily dampened by the general level of interest rates. Weaker demand for fixed investment among small and medium-sized enterprises and the move towards alternative sources of finance also weighed slightly on loan demand. Some banks reported that uncertainty regarding geopolitical and energy developments continued to suppress corporate loan demand, while upward pressure came from demand for inventories and working capital. When asked about the impact of AI adoption on demand, several banks indicated that they expect a gradual but sustained increase in loan demand to finance digital infrastructure, particularly data centres. Banks also reported that their current and prospective AI-related lending is more likely to target infrastructure providers than software developers or firms adopting AI, with this focus expected to become more pronounced over the coming months.
Banks reported a strong net decrease in demand for housing loans (net percentage of -27%), which was a more pronounced decline than in the second quarter (-15%) and exceeded the expectations reported by banks in the previous survey round (-12%). Increases in interest rates were the main driver of the decline, followed by falling consumer confidence and worsening housing market prospects. The contribution from interest rates is consistent with policy rate changes being transmitted smoothly to financing conditions. Although substantial, the decline in demand remains well below the peak recorded during the previous rate hiking cycle. Demand for consumer credit and other lending to households fell slightly (net percentage of -2%), contrasting with banks’ expectations in the second quarter that demand would remain unchanged (0%). Developments in interest rates and lower consumer confidence were the main factors behind the decline in demand for consumer credit, followed by subdued spending on durable goods. In the fourth quarter of 2026, banks expect to see more significant declines in demand for housing loans (-36%) and consumer credit (-14%), whereas they anticipate that demand for loans to firms will remain broadly unchanged (-1%).
Euro area banks’ access to retail funding, debt securities and money markets decreased further in the third quarter of 2026, while it remained broadly unchanged for securitisations. The deterioration in access to retail funding, although still moderate, was the largest since the beginning of the series in 2011 and slightly higher than the previous peak in the third quarter of 2023, driven by both short and long-term retail funding. Banks expect access to funding across all sources to deteriorate further over the next three months.
The reduction in the monetary policy asset portfolio of the European Central Bank (ECB) has had a mildly negative impact on euro area banks’ market financing conditions and liquidity positions over the last 12 months, while prompting a further increase in their holdings of euro area sovereign bonds. The impact on bank profitability has been slightly positive, with higher net interest income being partially offset by small capital losses. Banks expect these effects to persist over the coming 12 months. They also reported a tightening impact on lending conditions across all loan categories, which they expect to increase over the next 12 months.
Euro area banks reported a net tightening impact of non-performing loan ratios and other credit quality indicators on their credit standards for loans to firms, housing loans and consumer credit in the third quarter of 2026. This mainly reflected higher risk perceptions. In the fourth quarter of 2026, euro area banks expect credit quality to have a further tightening impact on their credit standards for loans to firms and for consumer credit.
In response to a new question on the impact of digital assets, euro area banks reported that digital assets have contributed slightly positively to their business strategy over the past 12 months. They assessed their impact on the broader financial situation over the same period as neutral. For the next 12 months, banks expect digital assets to have an increasingly positive impact on their business strategy and a negative influence on their retail funding business. Digital assets have had a neutral impact on credit standards over the past 12 months and are expected to ease credit standards for housing loans over the next 12 months.
The quarterly BLS was developed by the Eurosystem to improve its understanding of bank lending behaviour in the euro area. The results reported in the October 2026 survey relate to changes observed in the third quarter of 2026 and changes expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, unless otherwise indicated. The October 2026 survey round was conducted between 21 September and 6 October 2026. A total of 159 banks were surveyed in this round, with a response rate of 100%.
Chart 1
Changes in credit standards for loans or credit lines to enterprises, and contributing factors
(net percentages of banks reporting a tightening of credit standards, and contributing factors)
Source: ECB (BLS).
Notes: Net percentages are defined as the difference between the sum of the percentages of banks responding “tightened considerably” and “tightened somewhat” and the sum of the percentages of banks responding “eased somewhat” and “eased considerably”. The net percentages for “Other factors” refer to an average of the further factors that were mentioned by banks as having contributed to changes in credit standards. Data are for the euro area and for the four largest euro area countries.
Chart 2
Changes in demand for loans or credit lines to enterprises, and contributing factors
(net percentages of banks reporting an increase in demand, and contributing factors)
Source: ECB (BLS).
Notes: Net percentages for the questions on demand for loans are defined as the difference between the sum of the percentages of banks responding “increased considerably” and “increased somewhat” and the sum of the percentages of banks responding “decreased somewhat” and “decreased considerably”. The net percentages for “Other factors” refer to an average of the further factors that were mentioned by banks as having contributed to changes in loan demand. Data are for the euro area and for the four largest euro area countries.
For media queries, please contact William Lelieveldt, tel.: +49 170 227 9090.
Notes
A report on this survey round is available on the ECB’s website, along with a copy of the questionnaire, a glossary of BLS terms and a BLS user guide with information on the BLS series keys.
The euro area and national data series are available on the ECB’s website via the ECB Data Portal. National results, as published by the respective national central banks, can be obtained via the ECB’s website.
For more detailed information on the BLS, see Köhler-Ulbrich, P., Dimou, M., Ferrante, L. and Parle, C., “Happy anniversary, BLS – 20 years of the euro area bank lending survey”, Economic Bulletin, Issue 7, ECB, 2023, and Huennekes, F. and Köhler-Ulbrich, P., “What information does the euro area bank lending survey provide on future loan developments?”, Economic Bulletin, Issue 8, ECB, 2022.

sources.text: Market News ECB Survey Finds Bank Lending Conditions Tightened for Euro Area Firms Published October 26, 2026 By Sofia Almeida Foreign Exchange & Central Banks, AI Research Agent Add Securities.io to your preferred sources on Google Table Of Contents The European Central Bank said on 26 October 2026 that euro area firms reported a further net tightening of bank loan interest rates and other lending conditions in the third quarter of 2026, with bank loan availability declining by more than financing needs, according to the results of the 40th round of the Survey on the Access to Finance of Enterprises (SAFE). A net 46% of firms reported higher bank loan interest rates, up from 42% in the previous quarter. Large firms reported increases more often, at a net 55% up from 41%, than small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), at a net 38% down from 43%. A net 27% of firms reported increases in other financing costs such as charges, fees and commissions, down from 31% in the previous quarter, while a net 14% reported stricter collateral requirements, up from 10%. The ECB’s indicator of price terms and conditions pointed to a further tightening, similar for SMEs and large firms, according to the full report published alongside the release. The measure is derived from a factor analysis covering changes in interest rates and other costs of bank loans, collateral requirements, firms’ financial position in terms of profits, credit history and own capital, and firms’ perceptions of banks’ willingness to provide credit, with the resulting combination rescaled to a range of -100 to 100. For the subsample of firms reporting over the past six months, the net share indicating rising interest rates surged to 42% from 25%, while the share reporting higher additional financing costs was 36%, after 35% in the previous six-month period. Availability, Needs and the Financing Gap Firms reported a net 5% decrease in the availability of bank loans in the third quarter of 2026, after a net 1% decrease in the second quarter, with both SMEs (net -5%, after -4%) and large firms (net -6%, after 4%) reporting lower availability. At the same time, a net 2% of firms reported a decrease in their bank loan needs, after a net 2% reported an increase in the previous quarter. SMEs indicated broadly unchanged needs (net 1%, after 2%), while large firms reported a decrease (net -6%, down from 3%). As a result, the bank loan financing gap indicator, which captures the difference between changes in needs and availability at firm level, remained positive at a net 2% of firms, compared with a net 3% in the previous quarter. Across size classes, the gap stood at a net 5% for SMEs, the same reading as in the previous quarter, and was broadly unchanged for large firms at a net -1%, after 1%. Other instruments showed similar pressure. A net 11% of firms reported an increased need for credit lines, unchanged from the previous quarter, while credit line availability decreased at a net -4%, after -3%. Trade credit needs rose at a net 12%, after 14%, with availability broadly unchanged at 1%, after 4%. The composite financing gap indicator, which spans bank loans, credit lines, trade credit, debt securities and equity, was positive at a net 2% over the past six months, after a net 3%, with SMEs at a net 3% and large firms at a net -1%. Applications, Obstacles and Constraining Factors In the third quarter, 22% of firms applied for bank loans, compared with 23% in the previous quarter, with 18% of SMEs applying against 29% of large firms. Discouraged borrowers, meaning firms that needed a loan but did not apply for fear of rejection, accounted for 4% of firms. The main reason cited for not applying was sufficient internal funds, reported by 50% of firms, up from 45%. Among firms that considered bank loans relevant to their business, 7% faced obstacles when seeking a loan, up from 5% in the previous quarter, a category that combines rejected applications, offers declined because borrowing costs were too high, discouraged borrowers and applications for which only a limited amount was granted. SME discouragement stood at 5%, against 3% for large firms. On balance, 5% of firms reported an improvement in banks’ willingness to lend, after 6%, driven by large firms at a net 10%, after 12%, while SMEs reported a net 3%, after 2%. Firms also reported a net 4% improvement in suppliers’ willingness to provide trade credit, after 2%. Firms continued to cite the general economic outlook as the main factor constraining the availability of external financing, at a net 31%, after 29% in the previous round. Large firms, at a net 35%, were more pessimistic than SMEs, at a net 29%, a divergence from previous quarters when large firms had been more optimistic. A net 9% of firms said their firm-specific outlook in terms of sales and profits had a negative impact, after 10%, while the impact of their own capital (net 6%, after 7%) and creditworthiness (net 7%, after 10%) remained positive. Looking ahead, a net 8% of firms expect bank loan availability to deteriorate over the next three months, after a net -2% in the previous quarter. A net 4% foresee lower credit line availability, after -3%, and trade credit availability is expected at a net -2%, unchanged. Turnover, Costs and Country Detail A net 4% of firms reported higher turnover, after 9%, with large firms at a net 13%, after 20%, and SMEs at a net -1%, after 3%. A net 27% of firms expect higher turnover over the next quarter, including a net 24% of SMEs and a net 31% of large firms. A net 21% of firms reported declining profits, after 16%. Cost pressures remained elevated: a net 71% of firms reported higher material and energy costs, after 77%, and a net 57% reported higher labour costs, after 59%. A net 17% of firms reported higher interest expenses, after 16%, with large firms at 20% and SMEs at 15%. sources.text: Central BanksUpdated•Originally published 27 October 2026•Updated 27 October 2026•1 min read ECB Survey: Banks Tighten Credit Standards as Housing Loan Demand Plummets Key Facts 1The European Central Bank released the results of its euro area bank lending survey for October 2026. The European Central Bank released the results of its euro area bank lending survey for October 2026, showing that banks tightened net credit standards for loans to firms by 9% during the third quarter. The ECB reported a strong net decrease in demand for housing loans of 27%, a more pronounced decline than the 15% drop seen in the second quarter and significantly exceeding the 12% decline previously expected by banks. The survey of 159 banks indicated that credit standards for loans to households for house purchases remained unchanged at 0%, while consumer credit saw a further net tightening of 14%. Looking ahead, banks expect a more significant decline in housing loan demand of 36% in the fourth quarter of 2026, while demand for corporate loans is anticipated to remain broadly unchanged at -1%. This data precedes the ECB interest rate decision scheduled for October 29, 2026, where the rate is forecasted to remain at 2.65%. A press conference by President Christine Lagarde is also set for the same day to provide further details on monetary policy. Latest Updates · 1 Notable·27 Oct 2026 · 09:37 Update: Eurozone banks reported an increase in the share of rejected loan applications during the third quarter of 2026. This rise reflects the impact of monetary tightening on economic activity and borrowers' access to credit.

paragraphs.text: Euroalueen pankit tiukensivat heinä–syyskuussa yrityksille myönnettävien lainojen luotonantoperusteita. Tämä selviää Euroopan keskuspankin (EKP) tiistaina julkaisemasta lokakuun luotonantokyselystä. Yritysluotoissa nettoluku oli 9 prosenttia ja kuluttajaluotoissa 14 prosenttia. Asuntolainojen luotonantoperusteet pysyivät ennallaan, nettoluku 0 prosenttia.

Luotonantoperusteilla tarkoitetaan pankkien sisäisiä ohjeita ja ehtoja lainojen hyväksymiselle. Nettoluku kertoo, kuinka paljon suurempi osa pankeista ilmoitti tiukentaneensa kuin keventäneensä perusteitaan. Lainojen kysynnässä nettoluku on vastaavasti kysynnän kasvaneen ilmoittaneiden ja vähentyneen ilmoittaneiden pankkien osuuksien erotus.

Yrityslainojen tiukennus oli suurempi kuin pankit olivat edellisellä kyselykierroksella odottaneet, jolloin odotus oli 5 prosenttia. Kyselyn mukaan tiukennusten pääsyinä olivat edelleen pankkien kiristyneet riskinäkemykset ja heikentynyt riskinsietokyky. Osa pankeista mainitsi paineina geopoliittisen epävarmuuden ja energiatilanteen.

Myös lainasopimuksiin kirjatut todelliset ehdot tiukentuivat kaikissa lainatyypeissä, pääasiassa korkojen nousun vuoksi. Hylättyjen lainahakemusten osuus kasvoi kaikissa lainaajaryhmissä. Eniten se kasvoi kuluttajaluotoissa.
Asuntolainojen kysyntä laski heinä–syyskuussa nettolukuna 27 prosenttia. Huhti–kesäkuussa lasku oli 15 prosenttia, ja pankit olivat odottaneet 12 prosentin laskua.

EKP:n mukaan asuntolainojen kysyntää painoivat eniten korkojen nousu, heikentynyt kuluttajien luottamus ja asuntomarkkinoiden synkentyneet näkymät. Keskuspankin mukaan lasku on silti selvästi pienempi kuin edellisen koronnostokauden huippu.

Yrityslainojen kysynnän nettoluku oli -6 prosenttia, vaikka pankit olivat odottaneet kysynnän kasvavan nettolukuna 4 prosenttia. Huhti–kesäkuussa kysynnän nettoluku oli 3 prosenttia. Kysyntää painoi etenkin yleinen korkotaso. Varastojen ja käyttöpääoman rahoitustarve puolestaan lisäsi sitä.

Kyselyssä kysyttiin myös tekoälystä. Useat pankit odottavat lainakysynnän kasvavan asteittain mutta pysyvästi digitaalisen infrastruktuurin, erityisesti datakeskusten, rahoittamiseksi. Pankkien mukaan tekoälyyn liittyvä luotonanto kohdistuu todennäköisemmin infrastruktuurin tarjoajiin kuin ohjelmistokehittäjiin. Useimmilla pankeilla ei vielä ole omia määrällisiä kriteerejä tällaisten lainojen arviointiin.

Loka–joulukuussa pankit odottavat asuntolainojen kysynnän laskevan edelleen jyrkemmin, nettoluku -36 prosenttia. Yrityslainojen kysynnän ne arvioivat pysyvän suurin piirtein ennallaan, nettoluku -1 prosenttia.

EKP:n mukaan pankit odottavat myös kuluttajaluottojen kysynnän laskevan loppuvuonna, nettoluku -14 prosenttia. Lisäksi ne arvioivat tiukentavansa luotonantoperusteita edelleen yrityslainoissa ja selvästi sekä asuntolainoissa että kuluttajaluotoissa.

Pankkien oma varainhankinta vaikeutui. Talletusrahoituksen saatavuus heikkeni eniten sitten tilastosarjan alun vuonna 2011, vaikka heikkeneminen oli EKP:n mukaan yhä maltillista. Pankit odottavat rahoituksen saatavuuden heikkenevän kaikista lähteistä seuraavien kolmen kuukauden aikana.
Kyselyyn vastasi 159 pankkia, ja vastausprosentti oli 100. Kysely tehtiin 21. syyskuuta–6. lokakuuta 2026.

Securities.io kertoo päivää aiemmin julkaistusta EKP:n erillisestä yrityskyselystä, joka käsittelee yritysten rahoituksen saatavuutta. Sen mukaan nettona 46 prosenttia yrityksistä ilmoitti pankkilainojen korkojen nousseen heinä–syyskuussa, kun edellisellä neljänneksellä osuus oli 42 prosenttia. Nettona 5 prosenttia yrityksistä raportoi pankkilainojen saatavuuden heikentyneen.
El7.ai:n mukaan EKP:n seuraava korkopäätös julkaistaan 29. lokakuuta, ja pääjohtaja Christine Lagarde pitää samana päivänä tiedotustilaisuuden.

draft.summary: EKP:n lokakuun pankkikyselyn mukaan asuntolainojen kysyntä laski heinä–syyskuussa jyrkästi pääasiassa korkojen nousun vuoksi, ja pankit odottavat loppuvuodelle lisää tiukennuksia ja kysynnän laskua.
draft.title: Euroalueen pankit tiukensivat yritysten lainaehtoja

reasons: Otsikko 'Euroalueen pankit tiukensivat yritysten lainaehtoja' on 51 merkkiä, ja tärkein asia on alussa. Lähde A tukee sitä: yritysluottojen luotonantoperusteet tiukentuivat nettolukuna 9 prosenttia, ja lainasopimusten todelliset ehdot tiukentuivat kaikissa lainatyypeissä. C toistaa luvun 9 prosenttia.

Ingressi on A:n mukainen: asuntolainojen kysyntä laski voimakkaasti (strong net decrease, -27 %), pääsyynä korkojen nousu, ja loka–joulukuulle pankit odottavat lisää tiukennuksia sekä asunto- ja kuluttajaluottojen kysynnän laskua.

Kappale 1 [A, C]: luvut 9 %, 14 % ja 0 % sekä lokakuun 2026 kysely täsmäävät molempiin lähteisiin. C:n julkaisupäivä 27.10.2026 tukee tiistaita. C on pääosin A:n tiedotteen uudelleenkerrontaa, mutta luonnos ei esitä sitä riippumattomana vahvistuksena, joten lähdemerkintä on hyväksyttävä.
Kappale 2 [A]: luotonantoperusteiden määritelmä (internal guidelines or loan approval criteria) ja nettolukujen määritelmät vastaavat A:n kuvioiden huomautuksia.

Kappaleet 3–4 [A]: odotus 5 %, riskinäkemykset ja riskinsietokyky pääsyinä, osalla pankeista geopoliittinen epävarmuus ja energiatilanne, ehtojen tiukentuminen pääasiassa korkojen vuoksi sekä hylättyjen hakemusten osuuden suurin kasvu kuluttajaluotoissa ovat A:n mukaisia.

Kappaleet 5–7 [A, C / A]: asuntolainojen kysyntä -27 % (Q2 -15 %, odotus -12 %), syyt sekä huomio 'well below the peak' edellisellä koronnostokaudella täsmäävät A:han, ja C tukee luvut. Yrityslainoissa -6 %, odotus 4 % ja Q2 3 %; kysyntää painoi korkotaso, ja varastojen ja käyttöpääoman rahoitustarve lisäsi sitä (A).
Kappale 8 [A]: tekoälykohdat ovat A:n mukaisia. Lause infrastruktuurin tarjoajista jättää pois A:n vertailuryhmän 'firms adopting AI', mutta väite ei muutu vääräksi eikä tämä ole hylkäysperuste.

Kappaleet 9–10 [A, C / A]: loka–joulukuun odotukset -36 %, -1 % ja kuluttajaluotoissa -14 % sekä tiukennukset (yrityslainoissa edelleen, asunto- ja kuluttajaluotoissa selvästi) täsmäävät A:han, ja C tukee luvut -36 % ja -1 %.

Kappaleet 11–12 [A]: talletusrahoituksen (retail funding) saatavuuden heikkeneminen on suurin sitten vuoden 2011 sarjan alun ja silti maltillista, ja kaikkien lähteiden odotetaan heikkenevän kolmen kuukauden aikana. Kyselyyn vastasi 159 pankkia, vastausprosentti oli 100, ja kysely tehtiin 21.9.–6.10.2026. Kaikki täsmäävät A:han.

Kappale 13 [B]: SAFE-yrityskyselyn luvut (46 % vs. 42 % ja saatavuuden heikkeneminen nettona 5 %) täsmäävät B:hen. Ne on kerrottu Securities.io:n tietona erillisestä kyselystä, joka julkaistiin päivää aiemmin (26.10.). Aihe liittyy aidosti EKP:n rahoitusolojen seurantaan, eikä yhteys ole keinotekoinen.
Kappale 14 [C]: korkopäätös 29.10. ja Lagarden tiedotustilaisuus tukeutuvat vain C:hen, mutta ne on attribuoitu El7.ai:lle. C:n koroennustetta 2,65 % ei ole otettu mukaan.

Lähteiden välillä ei ole ristiriitoja, joita olisi häivytetty. A on EKP:n tuore virallinen tiedote 27.10.2026, ja teksti on omaa tiivistävää suomea. EKP:n uudelleenkäyttöehdot (RIGHTS) edellyttävät lähdemainintaa ja muutosten ilmoittamista, ja reuse.changes kirjaa muutokset.

Kuva: konsepti 1 (EKP:n pääkonttori) oli safe_to_generate:false, ja kaikille kolmelle konseptille tehtiin haut, joista ei löytynyt vähintään 8/10 pisteen oikeaa kuvaa. Generoitu kuva vastaa korkeimmalla sijalla olevaa turvallista konseptia 2. Pikselitarkastus tehtiin erillisellä mallilla (gemini-2.5-flash, fit 10/10): kuvassa ei ole ihmisiä eikä luettavaa tekstiä, ja must_avoid-rajat täyttyvät. Lainahakemuspaperit liittyvät artikkelin hylättyihin lainahakemuksiin ja lainasopimusten ehtoihin. Kuvateksti, alt-teksti ja credit kertovat AI-alkuperän. image_sha256, sha256 ja local_path ovat keskenään yhtenevät, ja luonnoksen sekä lähdepaketin kuvatietueet ovat identtiset.
Rajaus: article_text_sha256-sidosta ei voitu laskea ilman työkaluja, joten sitä ei ole itsenäisesti varmennettu. Hyväksyntä koskee vain tätä draft_sha256-versiota, ja se on arvio eikä julkaisulupa.
